ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram is a schematic diagram of an insect life cycle, with arrows connecting each stage in sequence. On the left, the one labeled F is the adult; near B at the top is the egg or early stage; on the right and below there are several oval nymph stages, developing in sequence along the arrows; the individual labeled H at the lower left is larger and has spiny legs, and is the last nymph form before entering the adult F. Reasoning: Fourth Instar Nymph refers to the fourth-instar nymph, usually the last nymph stage before the adult. In the diagram, the last nymph stage is located at H and is pointed by an arrow to the adult F. Therefore the fourth-instar nymph is at point H.
